topic: Notes on the foundations of mathematics, comparing the arithmetic of irrational numbers (Dedekind, Weierstrass, Cantor) with Euclidean geometry, and weighing two approaches: the geometric one and the analytic or genetic definition.

triage.modern_statement: This isn't a research question. Read in context, it asks which approach teaching ("Unterricht") takes when it introduces irrational/real numbers: the geometric route, based on Euclidean magnitudes, or the analytic/genetic construction (Dedekind cuts, Weierstrass, Cantor sequences). It is a remark about method and teaching. It cannot be stated as a mathematical proposition. The abbreviation 'Unterr.' and the uncertain reading add further doubt.
triage.answered_by: No answer as such. Hilbert later took up the related methodological contrast himself in 'Über den Zahlbegriff' (1900). There he set the genetic method used in arithmetic against the axiomatic method, and gave axioms for the real numbers modelled on his axiomatization of geometry. This is context only. No source links it to this diary entry.

evidence.claim: In 'Über den Zahlbegriff' (1900), Hilbert says the axiomatic way of proceeding is quite different from the genetic method used in arithmetic, and he sets out an axiom system for the real numbers (W. Sieg, 'The Ways of Hilbert's Axiomatics: Structural and Formal').

triage.why: The note asks which path instruction (Unterricht) takes. That is a question about how to teach or present the material, not an open mathematical problem. It is not one of the 23 problems or the 24th problem. The page's genetic-versus-geometric theme matches Hilbert's published 1900 discussion of genetic versus axiomatic methods, which suggests the note belongs to his thinking on method. I found no source that addresses this specific note. Confidence is not high because the reading of 'Unterr.' is uncertain.
